001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.jfr;
002
003import java.util.Locale;
004
005import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
006
007import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogAlerts;
008import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEvent;
009import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogFormatter.ThrowableFormatter;
010import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProperty;
011import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.EnumAlias;
012import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.LogConfigurable;
013import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.LogConfigurable.ConvertParameter;
014
015/**
016 * A {@link LogAlerts.Listener} that commits each alert as its own
017 * {@link RainbowGumAlertEvent} - deliberately a separate JFR event type family from
018 * {@link JfrLogOutput}'s {@link RainbowGumLogEvent}, even though the shape (per-level
019 * split, same fields) and rendering are the same; see {@link RainbowGumAlertEvent} for
020 * why sharing one event type between alerts and application log lines was rejected.
021 * <p>
022 * Alerts are rare and already delivered synchronously one at a time (see
023 * {@link LogAlerts#addListener(LogAlerts.Listener)}), so unlike {@link JfrLogOutput} this
024 * renders the message directly with {@link JfrLogOutput#MESSAGE_FORMATTER} instead of
025 * going through the buffered {@code LogEncoder}/{@code LogOutput} machinery meant for a
026 * high volume appender.
027 *
028 * @see JfrAlertListenerBuilder
029 * @see JfrAlertListenerConfigurator
030 */
031public final class JfrAlertListener implements LogAlerts.Listener {
032
033        private final Mode mode;
034
035        /**
036         * Whether alerts are committed as JFR events.
037         */
038        public enum Mode {
039
040                /**
041                 * Alerts are not committed as JFR events (the default).
042                 */
043                @EnumAlias("false")
044                OFF,
045                /**
046                 * Every alert is committed as a JFR event.
047                 */
048                @EnumAlias("true")
049                ON;
050
051                /**
052                 * Parses a property value: {@code on}/{@code true} or {@code off}/{@code false},
053                 * case insensitive.
054                 * @param value property value.
055                 * @return parsed value.
056                 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the value is not recognized.
057                 */
058                public static Mode parse(String value) {
059                        String v = value.strip();
060                        return switch (v.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)) {
061                                case "true" -> ON;
062                                case "false" -> OFF;
063                                default -> LogProperty.enumValue(Mode.class, v, "true", "false");
064                        };
065                }
066
067        }
068
069        /**
070         * Creates a JFR alert listener. Building one does not register it; see
071         * {@link JfrAlertListenerConfigurator}.
072         * @param mode whether this listener should be registered; see
073         * {@link JfrAlertListener#mode()}. Default {@link JfrAlertListener.Mode#OFF}.
074         * @return listener.
075         */
076        @LogConfigurable(name = "JfrAlertListenerBuilder", prefix = "logging.jfr.alerts.")
077        static JfrAlertListener of(@ConvertParameter("parseMode") @Nullable Mode mode) {
078                return new JfrAlertListener(mode == null ? Mode.OFF : mode);
079        }
080
081        static Mode parseMode(String value) {
082                return Mode.parse(value);
083        }
084
085        private JfrAlertListener(Mode mode) {
086                this.mode = mode;
087        }
088
089        /**
090         * Whether this listener should be registered with
091         * {@link LogAlerts#addListener(LogAlerts.Listener)}.
092         * @return mode.
093         */
094        public Mode mode() {
095                return mode;
096        }
097
098        @Override
099        public void onAlert(LogEvent event) {
100                var jfrEvent = newEvent(event.level());
101                if (jfrEvent == null || !jfrEvent.isEnabled()) {
102                        return;
103                }
104                var message = new StringBuilder();
105                JfrLogOutput.MESSAGE_FORMATTER.format(message, event);
106                jfrEvent.message = message.toString();
107                jfrEvent.logger = event.loggerName();
108                var t = event.throwableOrNull();
109                if (t != null) {
110                        var stackTrace = new StringBuilder();
111                        ThrowableFormatter.appendThrowable(stackTrace, t);
112                        jfrEvent.throwable = stackTrace.toString();
113                }
114                jfrEvent.commit();
115        }
116
117        /*
118         * Not a factory on RainbowGumAlertEvent itself: verifying a method of the event base
119         * class that returns its subclasses loads them while the base class is still being
120         * linked, and JFR fails to instrument an event class loaded then when a recording is
121         * already running (-XX:StartFlightRecording), leaving it uninstrumented or failing
122         * with a duplicate class definition.
123         */
124        private static @Nullable RainbowGumAlertEvent newEvent(java.lang.System.Logger.Level level) {
125                return switch (level) {
126                        case TRACE -> new RainbowGumAlertEvent.TraceEvent();
127                        case DEBUG -> new RainbowGumAlertEvent.DebugEvent();
128                        case INFO -> new RainbowGumAlertEvent.InfoEvent();
129                        case WARNING -> new RainbowGumAlertEvent.WarnEvent();
130                        case ERROR -> new RainbowGumAlertEvent.ErrorEvent();
131                        case ALL, OFF -> null;
132                };
133        }
134
135}
